newsitem.title: UK: China's communist system will collapse - Thatcher.
newsitem.headline: China's communist system will collapse - Thatcher.

text.p: Former British prime minister Margaret Thatcher said on Monday she was sure China's communist system would collapse as economic freedom spread.
"China has no history of liberty at all. She has always been under tyranny. She...(came) under communism in 1949. It will eventually collapse also," she told CNN in an interview.

"Communism will eventually collapse. indeed, it is starting. (Former leader) Deng Xiaoping realised it couldn't go on. So he said right -- economic liberty," said Thatcher, renowned for her opposition to communist systems when in power.
She was in power in 1984, when Britain signed the Joint Declaration with China spelling out how Hong Kong should be handed back to Beijing on July 1, ending 156 years of colonial rule.
"Beijing is so different from what it was in 1977. It has got the economic liberty," she said.
"It has not yet got a full rule of law...(although) law is coming too to China, initiative is coming to China, enterprise is coming to China. It won't stop."
Thatcher, speaking earlier to the BBC, said she felt both sad and proud that Britain was handing Hong Kong back to China.

"I hope the world recognises what Britain and everything we stand for has done for Hong Kong. This enormous prosperity -- those six and a half million people who built it under British administration -- is a great achievement,"
Asked how she felt as the last hours of British rule ticked away, the Iron Lady said: "Very sad -- tinged with pride."
Britain had turned a piece of barren land into one of the world's top trading centres with income per head greater than that in Britain, Thatcher said.

"This could not have been done without that magical combination of the great talent and ability of Chinese people, and tremendous hard work, coupled with British rule of law, British administration and a sense of equity and fair play.
Thatcher was forced to stand down as prime minister and leader of the Conservatives in 1990 by a party coup. She now sits in the House of Lords upper chamber of parliament.
